name: King's Indian Defense — Classical Variation
description: Black's most aggressive reply to 1.d4. Instead of contesting the center immediately, Black fianchettoes the bishop on g7 and allows White to build a broad pawn center — then counterattacks with ...e5 and ...f5. Fischer and Kasparov's weapon. White controls the board early; Black ignites the kingside later.

lines.name: King's Indian Defense — Classical Variation
lines.description: After 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 Bg7 4.e4 d6 5.Nf3 O-O 6.Be2 e5 7.O-O Nc6 8.d5 Ne7, both sides have staked out their plans. White holds a classical center with d5, c4, e4 and will push on the queenside. Black's fianchettoed bishop on g7 eyes the long diagonal, and ...f5-f4 is coming. Whoever breaks through first wins.
